lines.text: असिधारायां शयनमिव दुष्करं व्रतं the vow difficult like that of lying
on the edge of a sword. Cf. कण्टकव्रतशयनलीलाम् Kâd. p. 369.;
( 2 ) or as Malli. explains it ( Rag. XIII. 67. ) युवा युवत्या सार्धं
यत्सुग्धमधुरं वाचरेत् । अन्तर्निवृत्तसंगः स्यादसिधारं व्रतं हि तत् ॥ इति यादवः ।
इदं चासिधाराचंक्रमण ( moving on ) तुल्यत्वादसिधाराव्रतमित्युच्यते । Or (3)
according to some शयने मध्ये खड्गं निधाय स्त्रीपुंसौ यत्र ब्रह्मचर्येण स्वपत-
स्तत् । Or ( see com. ). This explains the extreme difficulty of
the course of conduct marked out for themselves by the good.

transcription.note: Several words in the Sanskrit quotation are difficult to distinguish.

lines.text: Sl. 29. An Anyokti. क्षाम-parched with; क्षै+कर्तरि कः । कृश—p.
p. of कृश् to be reduced; Pân. VII. 2. 55. शिथिलप्रायः—Almost
full of wrinkles, or decayed. N. B. At the end of a comp. प्राय
may be translated by ( 1 ) for the most part, almost; as मृतप्रायः
( 2 ) abounding or rich in, full of; as शालिप्रायो देशः; and
like, resembling; as वर्षशतप्रायं दिनम्. विपन्नदीधितिः—दीधिति means
तेजस् lustre, fire; hence vigour, energy.

transcription.note: The Sanskrit examples and grammatical derivation are somewhat unclear.

lines.text: मत्तेभेन्द्र—&c.—मत्ताः intoxicated, furious. कवल—a mouthful.
तस्य &c. whose desire is fixed solely on eating &c, मानमहताम्—
great by self-respect or honour. अग्रेसरः—अग्रमग्रेणाग्रे वा सरतीति
अग्रेसरः । ( see com. ). सूत्रेऽग्रे इति एदन्तत्वमपि निपात्यते । कथं तर्हि ‘यूथं
तदग्रसरगर्वितकृष्णसारम् ( Rag. IX. 55. ) इति । बाहुलकादिति हरदत्तः ।
Sid. Kau. The change of अग्र to अग्रे is irregular. केसरिन्—केसरः
अस्यास्तीति; as applied to the pollen of flowers, both केसर and
केशर are correct; but as applied to the mane of a lion केसर is the
only correct form. Hence केसरिन् is the only correct form and
not केशरिन् when meaning a lion ( as written in some lexicons ).

transcription.note: Some Sanskrit derivational text is difficult to read.

lines.text: Sl. 30. निर्मांस—The word मांस is curiously derived in Manu
Sm. V. 55. मां स भक्षयिताऽमुत्र यस्य मांसमिहाद्म्यहम् । एतन्मांसस्य
मांसत्वं प्रवदन्ति मनीषिणः ॥ अस्थिकं—a small bone; क in such cases
is used in a diminutive sense; it may also have a deprecatory
sense here; कुत्सितमस्थि अस्थिकम्. The reading अस्थि गोः has
no special propriety here. सिंहः—हिनस्तीति, a word of the पृषोदरादि
class; सिंहौ वर्णविपर्ययात् । Sid. Kau. सत्त्वानुरूपं worthy of, in
keeping with, one's greatness or magnanimity of heart, inherent

transcription.note: The Sanskrit derivation of सिंहः is not entirely clear.
